legacy_cells.I: 056_2025_CORTEX Composite Overlay for Risk Tiering and Exposure in Operational AI Systems.pdf
legacy_cells.FN: CORTEX organizes more than 1,200 AI incidents into 29 vulnerability groups within seven domains and proposes a five-layer risk scoring architecture. These taxonomy/scoring counts do not establish WM dynamics, predictive clinical effectiveness or calibrated prospective risk.
legacy_cells.FX: Title/abstract and introduction (printed pp. 1–2); literature review/background (pp. 3–5); methodology and scoring architecture (pp. 6–11); risk scorecard/results and relevant Tables 1–15 (pp. 11–31); conclusion and limitations (p. 32); remaining references and declarations (pp. 33–36). | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: This is a cross-sector AI risk-governance scorecard, not a healthcare world model; healthcare is mentioned as an example domain, not as the evaluated task. Table 14's result columns are partly misaligned in the extracted text, but that does not affect the exclusion/classification. A:I were left untouched. Evidence QA: 7/7 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (100%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 7 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 0 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: Model-assisted source review, no independent human review or verification of external standards/incident repositories.
No clinical cohort, clinical deployment, held-out event prediction or prospective validation. R1 refers only to technical scoring simulations.
Parameter normalization and k are inconsistent across equation, plots and table; no supplied code/seed resolves reproducibility.
Residual-risk direction in prose contradicts positive .15R coefficient; fixed modifier weights do not support unexplained vulnerability-specific sensitivity claims.
Counts and manual mapping of 1200+ incidents are claimed without incident-level extract, adjudication or coverage accounting.
